payload.goal: Add expense categories to the splitter. Extend the Expense type with an optional category field validated against a fixed set of categories, add computeCategoryTotals to the domain, expose listCategoryTotals from the API layer, render a category breakdown in the web surface, and cover the new behaviour with tests. Preserve the existing balance behaviour and keep the current tests green.

root.title: Add expense categories
root.objective: Add optional validated expense categories, category totals, API exposure, web breakdown rendering, and tests while preserving existing balance behavior.
expectedOutcomes: Expense category data is represented and validated in the domain.
Category totals are computable, exposed through the API, and visible in the web summary.

complexitySignals.rationale: The change crosses domain, API, web, and tests, with a public type/API extension but a small known file radius.

cut.rationale: The parent groups all category work because correctness depends on the domain model, aggregation, API exposure, rendering, and regression checks agreeing on the same category semantics.

children.title: Extend domain category model and totals
children.objective: Extend Expense with an optional validated category field and add computeCategoryTotals without changing existing balance computation semantics.
expectedOutcomes: Expense has an optional category field.
Invalid category values are rejected at the domain boundary used by existing expense creation or validation flow.
computeCategoryTotals returns totals grouped by category for categorized expenses according to the chosen uncategorized-expense policy.
Existing balance logic remains behaviorally unchanged.

complexitySignals.rationale: A small domain-file change with exported type/function impact and meaningful validation cases.

children.title: Expose category totals API
children.objective: Add listCategoryTotals in the API layer by delegating to the domain category totals function and preserving existing expense API behavior.
expectedOutcomes: listCategoryTotals uses the same category aggregation semantics as the domain.
Existing API exports and balance-related behavior remain compatible.

complexitySignals.rationale: This touches an exported API surface but should be a narrow delegation to domain logic.

children.title: Render category breakdown
children.objective: Update the web summary surface to render category totals alongside the existing balance summary without disrupting current balance display.

Category breakdown handles expenses with and without categories according to the accepted policy.
Existing balance summary remains visible and semantically unchanged.

complexitySignals.rationale: A focused web-surface change with moderate rendering-state and regression obligations.

children.title: Cover category behaviour

questions.question: What exact category values should the fixed category set allow?
questions.reason: The answer defines domain validation, API output, UI labels, and test fixtures.
options: Use a provided product category list
Adopt a small default set such as food, travel, housing, utilities, entertainment, other

questions.reason: The category field is optional, so aggregation and UI rendering need a deterministic policy.
options: Exclude uncategorized expenses from category totals
Include them under an Uncategorized bucket
